ground_truth.title: An Overview of Upcoming Tech Conferences in Atlanta in 2026
ground_truth.author: David Gracey
ground_truth.main_content:
Atlanta also has a strong and active technology community. The city’s startup hubs and corporate innovation centers offer a steady flow of tech talent. This is part of the reason why Atlanta tech conferences attract expert speakers who can share real-world experience.

“Atlanta’s mix of easy access, large venues, and active tech community also helps you turn conference time into follow-up results. You can meet regional service providers, find local talent, and set up on-site visits with nearby teams.” – David Gracey, Founder & President, Network 1 Consulting

If you’re an Atlanta-based business owner, there are a lot of good reasons to attend. If you’re like 75% of worldwide businesses facing a tech talent shortage, the right conference could be the ideal place for you to either find new talent or discover new ways to optimize your current resources. 

However, you need to know what’s coming up. To help you get started, this list will showcase some of the technology summits in Atlanta this year. We will also provide a quick chart of steps to take before you attend any of these conferences.

2026 Upcoming Tech Conferences in Atlanta, GA

1. Atlanta Science Festival (Celebrate STEAM)

Celebrate STEAM kicks off the Atlanta Science Festival on March 7, 2026, at Georgia Tech’s campus near the intersection of State Street and Ferst Drive. This high-energy day allows attendees to take part in hundreds of hands-on activities spanning robotics, nanotechnology, space science, and bioengineering.

2. Microsoft Fabric Community Conference (FABCON)

FABCON 2026 will be held from March 16 to March 19, 2026, at the Georgia World Congress Center. The event features over 100 deep-dive sessions and workshops led by the engineers who actually build the Microsoft Fabric platform.

3. Future Festival Atlanta

Future Festival is a one-day, AI-driven innovation conference designed to help business leaders navigate emerging consumer trends and disruptive technologies. The event will occur in multiple cities on multiple dates throughout the year, and will be in Atlanta on March 25, 2026.

4. 2026 Georgia Technology Summit

The Georgia Technology Summit, hosted by the Technology Association of Georgia (TAG), will take place on April 30, 2026, at the Cobb Convention Center (formerly known as the Cobb Galleria Center). The event brings together more than 1,000 technologists and business leaders from across the region. The summit is known for its “Top 40 Innovative Companies” exhibition and its focus on strengthening the local technology economy.

5. Atlanta Tech Week

Atlanta Tech Week celebrates the city’s vibrant startup culture with different neighborhoods hosting themed tracks each day. It aims to bridge the gap between early-stage founders, venture capitalists, and corporate innovators through mixers and panel discussions. The event will run from August 9 to August 14, 2026, at various locations across Atlanta.

6. Fintech South 2026

Fintech South 2026 will occur on August 18 and August 19, 2026, at the Woodruff Arts Center on Peachtree Street. This conference draws international banking and payment leaders to discuss the digital evolution of financial services. The agenda includes dedicated tracks for digital identity, blockchain integration, and the regulatory future of decentralized finance.

Tech Trade Shows in Atlanta in 2026

1. Southeast Design-2-Part Show

The Southeast Design-2-Part Show is an event for contract manufacturing, connecting engineers and purchasing agents with high-quality American suppliers. Visitors can explore a wide range of services, including 3D printing, CNC machining, and electronic assembly across hundreds of exhibit booths. The show will be held on March 10 and March 11, 2026, at the Cobb Convention Center.

2. RE+ Southeast

RE+ Southeast is set for March 31 and April 1, 2026, at the Georgia World Congress Center. This regional trade show focuses on the rapidly expanding renewable energy sector, specifically targeting solar energy and battery storage technologies. It provides a platform for clean-tech professionals to network with installers, developers, and utility companies to discuss the future of the power grid.

3. MODEX 2026

MODEX features more than 1,000 exhibitors showcasing the future of robotics and automated logistics. The show includes live equipment demonstrations and over 200 educational seminars focusing on “Supply Chains from Every Angle.” The massive expo runs from April 13 to April 16, 2026, at the Georgia World Congress Center.

4. Great American Franchise Expo

The Great American Franchise Expo serves as a major trade show for aspiring entrepreneurs looking to explore technology-enabled franchise opportunities across various industries. It features hundreds of franchisors and professional seminars on investment strategies, financing, and business operations for the modern owner. The show will take place on May 16 and May 17, 2026, at the Georgia World Congress Center.

5. TECHSPO Atlanta

TECHSPO is a high-energy technology expo that showcases the next generation of innovations in the realms of Mobile, AdTech, MarTech, and SaaS. This event is designed for marketers and developers to interact directly with new software products and hardware gadgets in an intimate setting. It is scheduled for June 3 and June 4, 2026, at the Westin Peachtree Plaza Hotel.

2026 Cybersecurity Conferences in Atlanta

1. Georgia Public Sector Cybersecurity Summit

The Georgia Public Sector Cybersecurity Summit will take place on March 18, 2026, in Atlanta (exact location to be determined). This specialized summit focuses on the unique security challenges faced by state and local government agencies and public educational institutions. Leaders gather to discuss incident response, inter-agency collaboration, and the protection of critical public infrastructure.

2. ManageEngine Shield NXG 2026

ManageEngine Shield is part of a national roadshow that focuses on the convergence of identity security and advanced threat defenses. Attendees will participate in expert-led keynotes and deep-dive sessions on unified security frameworks and SIEM capabilities. The roadshow’s Atlanta stop is scheduled for March 19, 2026, and will take place at Truist Park.

3. Level Zero Conference

The Level Zero Conference will be held from April 20 to April 22, 2026, at the SpringHill Suites by Marriott Atlanta Downtown. This event is dedicated to the security of industrial control systems (ICS) and operational technology (OT). The program features hands-on training for engineers and security professionals tasked with protecting physical assets from cyber-physical attacks.

4. CIOMeet: Atlanta 2026

CIOMeet is an exclusive gathering designed for senior IT executives and Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs) to discuss strategic leadership and cyber risk management. The event uses an intimate, interactive format to facilitate peer-to-peer networking and collaborative problem-solving for enterprise-scale security challenges. The meeting is set for August 27, 2026, and will take place at the Fogo de Chão in Dunwoody.

5. Global Security Exchange (GSX) 2026

GSX is a massive international event that bridges the gap between physical security and cybersecurity for professional security managers worldwide. The conference features over 200 educational sessions covering everything from drone security to enterprise-level digital risk mitigation and data privacy. This global summit will take place from September 14 through September 16, 2026, at the Georgia World Congress Center.

What to Do Before Attending Any Tech Events in Atlanta

What to Do Why It Matters
Set a clear goal Decide what you want to learn or solve before you register A clear goal helps you avoid sessions that do not support revenue, efficiency, or risk reduction
Review the agenda early Identify sessions tied to operations, growth, or technology planning Planning ahead saves time and keeps your focus on business impact
Research speakers and vendors Look up backgrounds, companies, and past talks This helps you prioritize credible experts and avoid sales-heavy sessions
Brief your internal team Ask your team what questions or gaps you should explore You return with answers that support real business needs, not personal curiosity
Schedule meetings in advance Book time with vendors or peers before the event starts Pre-set meetings prevent missed connections during a busy schedule
Define a budget limit Set spending limits for tools, services, and travel extras Budget control prevents impulse purchases driven by conference hype
Prepare evaluation criteria Write down how you will judge new tools or partners Clear criteria support better decisions after the event
Plan post-event follow-up Block time on your calendar to review notes and contacts Follow-up turns conference time into measurable business value

Ask Us How You Can Leverage What You Learned at IT Conferences

Whether you choose to attend one event or several, you will likely walk away with new ideas on how you can enhance technology within your organization. These ideas are great to have, but they won’t go far if you don’t have the resources to implement them.

If that’s where you’re stuck, you can reach out to Network 1 Consulting. Our Atlanta-based team is ready to help you roll out what you want.

and more!
